alex: Heads-up: I'm drafting a canonical benchmark spec for runtime perf. Need quick sync on metrics and harnesses. Main goals: apples-to-apples, repeatable, and catch regressions early. Thoughts?

sana: Love it. We should lock down these axes: model weights, tokenizer, decoding params, sequence length distribution, KV cache warmup rules, batching policy. TTFT vs TPOT definitions need a one-line canonical def.

mike: Suggested TTFT = time from request arrival to first token emitted (p50/p95/p99). TPOT = time to produce N tokens? Historically we've defined TPOT as 'time per output token' at steady-state. Should we define warmup exclusion window?

jordan: For replay harnesses we must replay real prefix lengths + cached k/v states. If we don't restore KV state then caching benefits won't show. Replay harness should include an option to 'load_kv=true' that replays KV from recorded sessions.

alex: Agree. Propose canonical: TTFT: wall-clock from request enqueue to first token emission (includes queueing). TPOT: median per-token latency measured after initial token (exclude first token) over the payload. Goodput measured as tokens/sec that match correctness threshold; QPS as requests/sec accepted. That distinguishes useful throughput vs raw.

chris: Important: quantization/kernel selection affects per-token jitter. We need to record kernel choices in bench metadata. Example keys: kernel_variant, cuda/cpu, int8/float16, seq_len, batch_size.

perf-bot: CI Alert: perf regression detected on canary 1844999900 -> p95 TTFT +18% for model 'vicuna-13b-q4' in nightly-run. Link: https://intranet/redwood/perf/1844999900

sana: :eyes: can we reproduce locally? Maybe due to batching heuristics change in the scheduler. Also check KV cache invalidation commit from yesterday.

mike: I ran a targeted replay and saw p95 TTFT up by ~20ms when batching cap changed from 16->8 under bursty arrival. Config I used: 
```json
{"batch_max":8,"batch_window_ms":3,"kv_warmup":true}
```
Full logs: s3://perf/logs/1845001.tar.gz

jordan: Also add steady-state definition: 'steady-state' = after 500 tokens or 2 seconds, whichever first. For TPOT compute only during steady-state.

alex: Good. Also require kernels prof: include per-kernel counters (matmul, softmax, RMS_norm) and GPU occupancy. Example snippet:
```bash
nvprof --metrics achieved_occupancy,flop_count_sp ... ./run_bench
```

chris: For apples-to-apples: same random seed, same sampling top_k/top_p, same batch packing strategy, and identical KV preload policy. We'll encode these in bench_config.json and reject runs missing fields.

sana: We should also define 'goodput' more precisely: tokens/sec for outputs that pass a correctness predicate (e.g., exact-match for eval prompts or BLEU/ROUGE thresholds). Goodput vs QPS: goodput counts tokens, QPS counts requests.

mike: One more: synthetic traffic should cover 3 profiles: steady, bursty (Poisson+bursts), and user-replay (trace-based). Each run annotated with seed, trace_id, and request size histogram.

alex: Let's put a PR with the canonical doc. Action items: sana draft TTFT/TPOT section; mike add harness configs + examples; jordan add KV replay guide; chris add profiler fields and required metadata. I'll open the PR by EOD. :rocket:
